Reviewed by the band

The band has now seen this work. Reported 2026‑08‑30: every member read the shared material and looked at the artwork. They like the wordmark, the skull, the year rings and the timeline, and they love the illustrated generated work.

That is a response to a direction, not a signature on each item. Individual artefacts, whether Böbbis becomes a standing per-release character, whether the skull is ever publicly named, and printing or selling anything are all still open. Where a direction was chosen inside a round, that was Marcus’s call.

Start with the plain-language overview if you haven’t already.

Blind spot: chosen by file formatBoth rounds built only from the two 2013 vectors that survived as parseable paths. The witty 1999–2003 era, closest to the platform's personality, was never a candidate because it survives only as raster.
Blind spot: thirty years carried by nothingBoth recommended primaries drop 1997–2027 entirely — the positioning's single un-copyable asset does no visual work anywhere.
Blind spot: nothing did a day's workEvery render in both rounds is a mark on an empty rectangle. No poster, avatar-in-circle, press page or light-ground proof existed before this round.

C1

The hazard sign system

constructed · 0 generationsthe genuine challenger

The 1999 Unbalanced cover taken seriously: a warning-sign language. One grammar — rounded triangle, inset ink ring, solid pictogram — and a different sign per subject: the falling figure (the primary; a band losing its footing in public since 1997), falling rocks (Get Stoned With Alexis), a sunrise (Tomorrow Is A New Day). Lamp Amber + Ink only — what thirty years does to hazard yellow. The joke is findable and never flagged; the register is roadside Finland, not folklore. Solves 16px natively — pictograms are designed for it.

96 circle
48 circle
  • Comedy cliff is real: one novelty pictogram would end it. Needs a written rule — real sign vocabulary only.
  • Skull-in-triangle was tested and rejected (too busy, two languages). Files kept as evidence.
  • At 16px it reads as a sign rather than the sign — still the best 16px candidate this round produced.
  • Adopting C1 as the identity retires the skull from the logo entirely — the biggest call on this page.
C2

Natural history — the label is the mark

4 generations + constructed labeladopt: the skull’s home

The skull reframed from metal icon to specimen: plate engraving and museum photography at large sizes — never shrunk, never a favicon — with the identity in the label: serif letterspaced APEZONE, a rule, Helsinki · est. Easter 1997. Every word on the label is documented fact; the generations were prompted wordless and came back wordless. No Latin, no plate numbers, no invented institutions — the round-1b fake caption has no descendant here.

  • An art-direction system with a label, not a logo system — owns no favicon, borrows a small-tier mark from C4 or C1.
  • Serif letterspaced caps drift toward boutique-gin if the plate world isn’t around them.
  • All generated images are 2026 pastiche and must never be presented as historical.
C3

The mark from the record

constructed · deterministic · 0 generationsnot a mark — adopt as furniture

No audio survives in this folder, so “a mark from the music” became a mark from the documented record: 31 years of public activity — 16 gigs, 23, at least 4, the silences, the garden — drawn to scale and nothing else. The rings read as tree rings or a pressed record around an Easter-1997 kernel; the pulse is the same ledger as a line. The thirty-first year hasn’t happened: it is always hollow, and it is the only warm thing.

  • The brief’s suspicion was right: it fails as a mark. The rings die at 96px; mono survives but only where large sizes already work.
  • The encoding needs its one-sentence caption, once, findable — like the Kivi sentence.
  • Verdict: large-format anniversary artefact (poster, vinyl, backdrop) and the pulse absorbed into C5 as system furniture. Competes for no tier.
C4

Non-pictorial — the Λ–Z device

constructed · 0 generations · tests decision 1adopt: the small tiers

APE|ZONE splits at its seam into Λ and Z — set heavy (26% stroke, siding with round B against A's thin spec), with an en dash between: everything from Λ to Z, rhyming typographically with 1997–2027. The dash is the only warm element — a colour rule, not a decoration. The Λ is crossbarless on purpose: the one “wrong” thing kept, inherited from the band’s own 2013 letterforms — the visual semiapes. This tests decision 1 openly and concludes the wordmark survives as the mark; the device takes only the tiers the 7.92:1 wordmark physically cannot occupy.

96 circle
48 circle
  • “A–Z” is a crowded idea (guides, Amazon’s arrow); ownability rests on the crossbarless Λ, the weight and the amber dash, and needs a name-covered test against other A/Z marks.
  • The nested variant failed — a trinket, kept as evidence.
  • A bare Λ at 16px is generic; the claim is “best available”, not “distinctive”.
C5

Identity as a system, not a mark

constructed · 0 generations · absorbs provocation 4adopt: the grammar

No logo. A grammar: the record line (APEZONE · HELSINKI · 1997–2027, amber dash), the stamp, date furniture set huge (the band’s real places and dates are the imagery), the pulse rule from C3 — one warm element per surface, no exceptions. Demonstrated on the artefacts the audiences actually meet, which no round had built before: a gig poster, an archive post, a press header. The joke lives in the voice, where the platform says it belongs. All copy is placeholder voice-pattern; the poster date is Easter Sunday 2027 as a specimen — no gig is booked.

  • Owns no favicon and doesn’t pretend to — pairs with C4’s Λ or C1’s sign.
  • A grammar needs an enforcer: without a one-page rule sheet it decays into “some DIN posters”.
  • Bahnschrift is placeholder; authority depends on task 2.3 delivering real mass.
C6

Break the brief on purpose

4 generations + loud type · the licensed exceptionbrief confirmed

The one direction licensed to violate restraint reads as confidence — built as the best possible loud, not a strawman. The generator, fed only the band’s skull and a maximalist brief, reassembled skull + stars + chains — the 2011 badge vocabulary — upgraded in craft. It is genuinely good, and it is unmistakably a younger band. Beside it the restrained work reads more confident: the brief is confirmed by evidence rather than assertion. The nuance worth keeping: loud has a legitimate home as occasional artefact (a screen-print, a tour shirt) inside a restrained system — never as the system.

The hybrid remix — Marcus's mid-session ask

The same loud worlds rebuilt around round B's reduced jawless mark instead of the anatomical skull. The generator held the mark's silhouette almost exactly — and the reading changes: this is no longer a different band, it is the band's own mark having a loud day. The usable formula: quiet mark, loud frame — the mark never goes maximal, the environment may, on one-off artefacts. (The stars + skull pairing remains decision 6's forbidden 2011 combination — deliberate here, to be re-read before any real use.)

  • Everything here is generated concept mood; the type is placeholder.
  • The star elements sit one step from the 2011 badge — decision 6 forbids that reassembly in real use.
  • Competes for no tier; exists for the comparison, and the comparison is done.

Verdict

As the primary mark, no — round A’s Direction 1 still wins, with one correction: the letterforms must be redrawn genuinely heavy (round B was right; A’s thin spec was the error the “convergence” concealed).

But the standing system loses three parts to this round. The skull leaves the small tiers — C4’s Λ–Z takes favicon and avatar (the only artefact in three rounds that survives the whole ramp). The skull gets the job it is actually good at — C2’s plates and specimens. And C5’s grammar (record line, date furniture, one-warm-element rule, pulse) is adopted around whatever mark wins, filling the in-context gap every previous round left open.

One genuine challenger stands: C1. It competes on a different premise — identity as sign language — and it is the only direction in three rounds that houses the humour and the Finnishness the platform demands. Adopting it is a positioning decision, not a measurement; the workable middle path is the sign grammar as the release-and-gig pictogram programme inside a wordmark-led identity. C6 confirmed the restraint brief on evidence. Full reasoning and the recommended assembly: VERDICT.md.

Honesty notes

  • Concepts for choosing a direction — not deliverable artwork. Constructed marks use placeholder type (Bahnschrift, Georgia); the final letterforms are task 2.3’s job.
  • Generated (Freepik, reference-guided on the band’s own marks): C2’s four images, C6’s four, and four hybrid remixes on round B’s reduced mark — 12 generations total. Nothing generated is archival, historical, or a logo.
  • No fabricated captions anywhere: C2’s label carries documented facts only; the C5 poster’s date is a specimen (Easter Sunday 2027), not a booking; all copy is voice-pattern placeholder.
  • Provocations 4 (anniversary as mark) and 7 (wordless) were dropped with reasons — see README.md.
  • Not tested: physical size, fabric, CMYK, blur/distance abuse, and the name-covered ownability sheet — the honest next sessions.
  • Data in C3: gig counts and events from notes/band-facts.md; 2001 is “at least 4”; the 1998/1999 Unbalanced year conflict is noted, counted once in 1999.
